page: Amazon Web Services m7i.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processor with 32 vCPUs, corresponding to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in specific computational and memory tasks. The instance achieved strong ratings in Geekbench single-core (2048.0) and multi-core (16303.0) tests, alongside strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression (32.91 GB/sec) and static web serving throughput (46.4 GB/sec). Memory performance is supported by high-speed DDR5, yielding a cached read-only small block bandwidth of 2631.1 GB/sec. For machine learning workloads, the hardware-assisted AMX instructions enable top-tier text generation speeds of 413.98 tokens/second on small LLM models (135M) and strong prompt processing speeds of 175.93 tokens/second on medium models (7B).

Lacking local NVMe storage, the m7i.8xlarge relies entirely on network-attached storage, which represents a tradeoff for workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space. However, its balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio and robust cryptographic and vector instruction sets make it highly cost-efficient for general-purpose enterprise workloads. It is well-suited for static web serving, application servers, software compilation, and moderate-scale machine learning inference tasks that leverage CPU-based matrix acceleration.
description: The Amazon Web Services m7i.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by a dedicated 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8488C processor. It features 32 vCPUs, 128.0 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory, and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Running on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance supports advanced CPU instruction sets including Intel AMX and AVX-512, which drive strong performance in cryptographic, compression, and vector-based workloads. Benchmarks show strong results in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, static web serving throughput at 46.4 GB/sec, and top-tier text generation for small LLM models. Lacking local storage and dedicated GPUs, this instance offers a balanced resource profile, making it a cost-efficient choice for enterprise applications, software compilation, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
